Decarbonisation of the Power sector in a resource-constrained geography: Assessing the pathway for Goa

India's achievement of the net-zero target by 2070 depends heavily on the policy direction that the states take in transforming and decarbonising their power sector. The planning and implementation of this transition is particularly challenging for resource-constrained states. Goa demonstrates this problem clearly. With limited land resources, an environmentally sensitive ecosystem and inconsistent wind resources throughout the year, Goa has traditionally relied on other states and central thermal power stations to meet around 75 per cent of its electricity demand, with thermal power comprising a bulk (80 per cent) of the procured power. To decarbonise its power demand, Goa can procure power from renewable projects located outside the state. However, this approach continues the state's dependency and can expose it to external supply and price risk. In this context, this paper examines the pathway, considering both a centralised and decentralised approach, for the state to decarbonise its sector while building its internal generation capacity to meet its growing demand.
The assessment will use a mixed-method approach to analyse power demand growth alongside available renewable resources within the state, considering solar potential, wind variability, energy storage potential, and biomass availability. The analysis is aimed at identifying a mix of technologies that are financially feasible in terms of levelised cost, suitable to Goa's geography, and can support the state in reducing its reliance on thermal and outside-the-state procurement. The approach and framework will also help other resource-constrained states plan the decarbonisation of their power sector.

Keywords: Power sector decarbonisation, renewable potential, Goa, thermal, resource-constrained.
